purpose: Determine, independently of the prior OECD missing-row result, whether ESA 2010 supplies an authoritative semantic treatment for the S1M / liabilities / F2 cell before any new numerical value gate is opened.

official_source.title: European system of accounts — ESA 2010
official_source.normative_role: Canonical ESA 2010 institutional-sector and financial-instrument definitions used by European financial accounts.

exact_references.semantic_point: Currency F.21 consists of notes and coins issued or authorised by monetary authorities.
Deposits F.22/F.29 are standardised non-negotiable contracts offered by deposit-taking corporations and, in some cases, central government as debtors.
Transferable deposits predominantly represent liabilities of resident deposit-taking corporations, in some cases central government, and non-resident institutional units.
An overdraft beyond a deposit balance is classified as a loan, not as a negative deposit.
All resident sectors and the rest of the world may hold transferable deposits; this establishes holder-side universality, not issuer-side universality.
The central bank S.121 is a financial-corporation subsector whose principal functions include issuing currency.
Deposit-taking corporations except the central bank are classified in S.122 and are defined by receiving deposits and/or close substitutes from institutional units.
S.14 households are a distinct institutional sector; deposit-taking corporations are not classified in S.14.

independence_from_prior_result.rule: The applicability conclusion must stand from ESA definitions even if the OECD row had been present.
